flashcards.back: Both can represent nested semi-structured data; XML uses tags, while JSON uses objects, arrays, and key–value pairs.
Flexible ingestion delays some schema and validation work until query time.
Joins, grouping, and sorting may shuffle data across partitions even when the SQL is short.

homework.prompt: Choose relational, XML, or JSON for three workloads and justify each choice by structure and constraints.
homework.rubric: Name nesting/variation, stable identity, validation timing, and consumer needs.

homework.prompt: Design a measurement plan for a distributed query whose average runtime is acceptable but one partition is slow.
homework.rubric: Measure partition sizes, skew, shuffle bytes, and stage/barrier time.
